sentences.text:
(PER: HON'BLE MRS JUSTICE M G UMA) The petitioners being accused Nos.1 to 3 in Crime No.72/2021 of Women Police Station, Yadgir, (C.C.No.319/2022 pending on the file of the learned Civil Judge and CJM, at Yadgir), registered for the offence punishable under Sections 323, 498-A,
504, 506 r/w 34 of IPC, are seeking to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against them.
2. Heard Sri. Shivshankar S.K., learned counsel for the petitioners and Smt.Arati Patil, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent - State.
Perused the materials on record.

3. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the criminal proceedings initiated against the petitioners is liable to be quashed invoking inherent power under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023?"
NC: 2025:KHC-K:4442 HC-KAR 4.

My answer to the above point is in the 'Negative' for the following:
REASONS 5.

The facts of the case in brief are that, respondent No.2 as informant filed the first information against accused Nos.1 to 7 which was registered in Crime No.72/2021 of Women Police Station,
Yadgir, alleging commission of offence punishable under Sections 323, 498-A, 504, 506 r/w 34 of IPC.
The investigation was undertaken and final report came to be filed.
The Trial Court took cognizance of the offence and registered C.C.No.319/2022.
The petitioners being accused Nos. 1 to 3 are seeking to quash the criminal proceedings against them.

6. During the course of addressing the arguments, the attention of the Court was drawn to the order dated 08.02.2022 passed in Criminal Petition No.201737/2021 filed by accused No.1 to 7 seeking to quash the criminal NC: 2025:KHC-K:4442 HC-KAR proceedings initiated against them.

The co-ordinate Bench of this Court on consideration of the allegations made against the accused,
formed an opinion that the criminal proceedings against accused Nos.4 to 7 is liable to be quashed.

However, a categorical finding was recorded that the petitioner Nos.1 to 3 being accused Nos.1 to 3 were residing with the victim under the same roof and there are sufficient materials on record to proceed with the matter and accordingly the petition was allowed in part quashing the criminal Lalith And Ors vs State Of Karnataka And Anr on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7647728/
3 proceedings against accused Nos.4 to 7 while rejecting the claim for quashing against the petitioners herein.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. Admittedly, after dismissal of the petition filed by the petitioners in Criminal Petition No.201737/2021, the final report came to be filed by the Investigating Officer by recording the statement of various witnesses.
Now again the petitioners are before this Court seeking to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against them.

When the co-ordinate Bench of this Court had already NC: 2025:KHC-K:4442 HC-KAR formed an opinion that there are prima-facie materials against the petitioners to constitute the offence under Section 498-A, 323, 504, 506 r/w 34 of IPC
, once again this Court cannot take a re-look into allegations to form a different opinion.
It is also pertinent to note that now in view of filing the final report by the Investigating Officer, more prima facie materials are placed before the Court to constitute the offence.
8. In view of the above, the petitioners are not entitled for grant of relief.
I do not find any reasons to quash the criminal proceedings.

Accordingly, I answer above point in the negative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is dismissed.

Sd/-
